Latin word

acadēmīa

acadēmīa, acadēmīae f.

noun, first declension

a university

In this lexicon

  • university

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. school types: university, after Vives (1540), Mercator (1595) and Tursellinus (1652); Traupman 28, 267 (academy)

Notes

  1. 1acadēmīa: long i (Traupman 28 and Morgan–Owens acadēmia). Cicero’s own verse scans it long: Inque Acadēmīā umbriferā nitidōque Lycēō (Div. 1.22), where -dēmī- makes a spondee before the elided final -ā. Lewis & Short: long in Cicero and in Tullius Laurea (ap. Plin. NH 31.8), short only in Claudian and Sidonius. Greek Ἀκαδήμεια.

Examples

  • in Valentīnā Acadēmīā (ūniversitātem vocant) tōtō orbe celeberrimā

    at the Academy of Valencia (they call it a university), the most famous in the whole worldRuiz (1794), p. viii, quoted by Morgan–Owens s.v. school types: university
